title: Wrap paragraph prose around simple bare template expressions
description:
Ordinary paragraphs containing simple bare expressions such as `{{ foo }}` can now reflow while preserving each expression byte-for-byte. Real links and surrounding emphasis receive normal formatting. Explicit targets rejected solely for these expressions can now succeed.

Base: `42efa88769b13a6df75bb669b7f492b19d5a70e6`, the fetched `origin/main`. Ancestry checks confirm it includes #7 (`e141e9d`), #8 (`f66599a`), and #9 (`42efa88`).

With `--wrap sentence`:

```diff
-First
-sentence with {{ foo }}. Second
-sentence.
+First sentence with {{ foo }}.
+Second sentence.
```

With `--canonical --wrap sentence`:

```diff
-First
-sentence with {{   user.name   }} and [real](  target  ). Second
-sentence with _outside_.
+First sentence with {{   user.name   }} and [real](target).
+Second sentence with *outside*.
```

The exception requires the effective delimiters to include the exact `{{` / `}}` pair. The lexical subset is an ASCII identifier (`[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`), optionally followed by `.NAME` components, surrounded by optional ASCII spaces or tabs inside the braces. The expression must occupy one physical line at the top level of an ordinary paragraph. Before it, require whitespace or a paragraph boundary; after it, require whitespace, a paragraph boundary, or `. , ; : ! ?`. Every other template occurrence must be another eligible bare expression or a code-contained occurrence already supported by #9.

Standalone lines containing one or multiple bare expressions retain baseline preservation. Reflow also falls back when the existing layout would create such a line. Expressions remain indivisible; there is no special packing algorithm. Quoted, nested, attached-word, shortcode, and other complex expressions retain existing behavior. Raw-angle ambiguity, apparent hard breaks, multiline constructs, and inconsistent literal boundaries remain excluded. Disabled/replaced delimiters, parent/container guards, Markdown-in-YAML, and source-language handling retain their existing policies.

Internally, `ParagraphCodeSpans` becomes `ParagraphTemplateSpans`, retaining distinct code-content and bare-expression ranges recognized on the original source. Initial planning, explicit-target validation, and effective-policy finalization share this recognition. Delimiter changes reuse those ranges. Existing balanced-brace protection preserves the expression through normalization, canonicalization, and wrapping. A retained line flag records template-only placement before token coalescing; the planner checks it before accepting a layout. Emission and global template detection are unchanged.

Eight new CLI transcripts record the required examples, mixed code/bare content, column wrapping, narrow fallback, standalone lines, complex controls, and explicit-target/skip behavior. Five positive transcripts fail on the recorded base and pass on the branch; all eight pass on both first and second branch passes. Focused CLI tests cover identifiers, exact spaces/tabs, wrapping modes, canonicalization, delimiter configuration and late directives, targets, skips, and compatibility boundaries.

Three existing expectations change deliberately:

- `markdown_template_code_boundaries.case`: its first paragraph now reflows because `{{ outside }}` is an eligible inline bare expression. All remaining paragraphs are unchanged.
- `ambiguous_or_non_code_templates_keep_the_original_paragraph`: the same mixed code/bare row now formats under eligible layouts; narrow layouts still preserve it.
- `explicit_targets_keep_other_rejections_and_skip_precedence`: `Before {{ foo }}.` now succeeds. Other diagnostics and skip precedence remain unchanged.

Validation passed: `cargo test --test cli_cases`, the focused bare/code paragraph suites, and the unchanged `scripts/check.sh` (format checking, Clippy with warnings denied, Rust tests, 153 external tests, and 57 VS Code tests).

Both executables were built with `cargo build --bin yamark` using Rust 1.98.1 and the same default development profile. Differential comparison covered stdout bytes, stderr, and exit status for all 88 existing CLI fixtures, 77 applicable second passes, and 784 focused combinations. The only changed existing fixture is the deliberate mixed paragraph above; there were no unexpected differences. All 170 changed focused combinations were idempotent and retained expression bytes. Temporary 1,000/4,000/16,000-expression and malformed-opener probes showed no new repeated-suffix growth; no benchmark framework was added.

The contract is exact expression preservation within this fixed lexical and placement subset. It does not claim general template-language support, complete CommonMark recognition, or equivalent rendering across template engines. Narrow layouts may intentionally remain unchanged. #8/#9 code-only regressions are unchanged.

Refs #2

title: Wrap paragraphs with template text inside inline code
description:
Paragraphs containing template delimiters inside complete, single-line inline code can now receive normal whitespace, link, canonicalization, and wrapping changes. The code contents stay exact. Refs #2. Bare-template reflow remains separate.

Base: `f66599a0b24203e32580b8bb9f652f6c4968e641`, the latest `origin/main` when this branch started. Both #7 (`e141e9d0124925e37954554c8f85b0190d252099`) and #8 are merged into this base.

With `yamark format --wrap sentence --stdin-file-path input.md`, the issue example changes from:

```markdown
First
sentence with `${{ foo }}`. Second
sentence.
```

to:

```markdown
First sentence with `${{ foo }}`.
Second sentence.
```

The combined code/link example changes from:

```markdown
First
sentence with `{{ foo }} [x](  url  )`. Second
sentence with [real](  target  ).
```

to:

```markdown
First sentence with `{{ foo }} [x](  url  )`.
Second sentence with [real](target).
```

Each input and output ends with LF. Both required examples fail on the recorded base and pass here. An overwide code span remains intact; `--wrap none` retains its normal no-reflow behavior while eligible link and canonical formatting can run.

Eligibility is limited to ordinary paragraphs whose configured template delimiter occurrences pair within complete top-level code spans on individual source lines. The paragraph itself can span lines. Single backticks and unambiguous longer delimiters use the existing recognition rules. Escaped, unmatched, or inconsistent backtick runs, crossing pairs, stray delimiter occurrences, nested code contexts, multiline literals, apparent hard breaks, and ambiguous math boundaries retain template preservation. No template-language quote parsing is added.

Template text in bare prose, math, HTML, link destinations, or attributes remains protected. Unescaped raw `<` outside consumed constructs rejects the exception; `<` inside eligible code does not. The #8 link normalizer and its raw-angle stop are unchanged. Heading, table, container, footnote, shortcode, YAML, and source-language policies remain unchanged. Existing Markdown divs and Markdown fences already contain parsed child documents, so their ordinary child paragraphs benefit naturally; host/container guards are not relaxed to reach them.

Internally, `RetainedMarkdown` lazily keeps `ParagraphCodeSpans`: compact offsets into the original source, or a recorded ambiguous classification. Recognition reuses `InlineScan` and the existing span helpers in source order. Initial planning, explicit-target validation, and finalization share `preserves_templates`. Policy checks reuse those original ranges as delimiters change; an earlier check that did not encounter the template guard has no classification to reuse. Global template detection, front-matter options, scoped state, and skip/error precedence retain their existing semantics. The metadata is released with recognition drafts before prepared-plan emission.

Five new CLI transcripts record exact arguments, stdin, stdout, stderr, and status:

- `markdown_template_code_issue_2.case`
- `markdown_template_code_links.case`
- `markdown_template_code_narrow.case`
- `markdown_template_code_target.case`
- `markdown_template_code_boundaries.case`

Thirteen parameterized CLI tests cover default/custom/replaced delimiters, multiple pairs and spans, wrap modes, canonicalization, literal bytes, second passes, directive changes, explicit targets, and compatibility boundaries. The only changed pre-existing expectation is #8's ordinary paragraph containing `` `[x](  url  ) {{ value }}` ``: its real link, outside emphasis, and wrapping now format while the code remains exact. All other #8 regressions and existing transcripts remain unchanged.

`cargo test --test cli_cases` and the unchanged `scripts/check.sh` pass: formatting, Clippy, 636 Rust tests, 153 external tests, and 57 editor tests. There are 88 passing CLI transcripts. Base and branch release binaries were built with Rust 1.98.1 and equivalent `cargo build --locked --release` settings in separate target directories.

Differential replay covered 887 inputs and 2,097 first/second-pass comparisons of stdout bytes, stderr, and exit status. The 658 differences are confined to eligible paragraphs, their surrounding formatting, and authorized target acceptance. All 83 pre-existing transcripts match the base. Among the five existing documentation fixtures, only the paragraph listing default delimiters in `website/reference-config.qmd` changes. Changed first-pass outputs are stable on their next pass. Temporary guards at 62 function entry points passed on all 887 inputs without entering recognition, template scanning, or raw-source formatting during emission. Temporary scaling checks covered long paragraphs, up to 65,536 code spans/delimiter candidates, and unmatched braces, brackets, backticks, and emphasis; no new repeated-suffix growth was observed.

Two boundary effects are explicit in the regressions and differential review. A target accepted before a late file delimiter directive can subsequently be preserved by that directive; it no longer fails solely because its original policy saw a template inside code. Also, main already strips apparent hard-break spaces during final cleanup of preserved paragraphs. This first-pass behavior remains unchanged, but the cleaned source can become eligible on a later invocation.

This does not provide complete CommonMark code-span recognition or general template/HTML support. Bare templates and ambiguous inputs retain the existing guard. PRs #4 and #6 are unchanged.

title: Preserve inline literals and skip ambiguous link rewrites
description:
Link/image normalization can strip spaces from link-looking text inside recognized inline code or math. This change preserves those literal contents while continuing to normalize real links outside them. For ambiguous raw-angle inputs, it conservatively skips link/image normalization.

Base: `e141e9d0124925e37954554c8f85b0190d252099`.

With `--wrap paragraph`:

```text
Input:
Before `[x](  url  )` after [real](  target  ).
Before $![x](  image  )$ after ![real](  target  ).

Output:
Before `[x](  url  )` after [real](target).
Before $![x](  image  )$ after ![real](target).
```

The normalizer visits existing code/math spans and atomic link/attribute constructs in source order. If it reaches an unescaped `<` outside those consumed constructs, it discards any partial normalization and returns its original input. Ordinary less-than signs, autolinks, and incomplete angle syntax all trigger this conservative rule. Escaped `<` and angle syntax inside already-consumed literals, link destinations, or attributes do not.

The unit preserved by this pass is the source string supplied by its paragraph or segment caller. Link/image normalization is skipped throughout that unit, including real links before and after the angle marker. Existing whitespace handling, canonicalization, and wrapping still run; independently eligible paragraphs still normalize links.

```text
Input:
Before `[a](  u  )` < value then `[b](  v  )` after [r](  t  ).

Output:
Before `[a](  u  )` < value then `[b](  v  )` after [r]( t ).
```

Both code spans retain their contents. The real link retains padding because link normalization was skipped; the existing whitespace pass reduces its repeated spaces. This is preservation during link normalization, not a promise to copy the entire paragraph verbatim.

The production change is confined to `src/core/wrap.rs`. It reuses the existing recognition rules and adds a lazy code-span cache to avoid repeated failed suffix searches. All recognition and normalization remain in planning; #7's prepared-document emission boundary is unchanged. No HTML interpretation or retry without literal protection is added.

Six CLI transcript cases record exact arguments, stdin, stdout, stderr, and exit status. Fifteen parameterized CLI tests add wrap-mode, canonicalization, emphasis, container, escape, overwide-literal, template, unmatched-opener, and second-pass coverage. `AGENTS.md` now requires transcript cases for public-facing behavior changes.

Intentional output differences are retained literal contents, retained link padding in ambiguous inputs, and resulting wrapping changes. The PR's mixed-angle assertions reflect that preservation policy, including links in attributes/comments and before/after malformed angle candidates. Existing fixtures from base remain unchanged. HTML helpers, the support scanner, template policy, public APIs, dependencies, CI, and test infrastructure are unchanged.

`scripts/check.sh` passed: formatting, Clippy, 623 Rust tests, 153 external tests, and 57 editor tests. All 83 CLI transcripts pass. The latest differential replay compared 3,431 inputs with `3a1df5e`; all 1,564 changed outputs followed the conservative preservation path, with no unexplained differences or new second-pass instability. Temporary emission guards and long-input scan checks passed. GitHub CI also passed for `347b17d`.

Existing recognition limitations remain, including the backtick matcher's acceptance of part of a longer closing run. This PR does not promise complete CommonMark/HTML recognition or general multiline-literal preservation. It does not resolve issue #2 or change template preservation.

title: Refactor Markdown formatting to consume retained plans
description:
Retain Markdown planning results so paragraph and container emission no longer repeats recognition or rebuilds fragment source. This is an internal refactor intended to preserve CLI output, support decisions, fallbacks, configuration semantics, diagnostics, and exit status.

Main baseline: `bfa7c7b6446e3ab870bd54daf8d6962f5a944343`.

```text
main:
  parse -> trial-format support probe -> discard output
  emit -> raw formatters -> decode/parse/emit fragments

with this change:
  parse -> ParsedDocument owns source and drafts
  finalize(self, options) -> PreparedDocument owns source and plans
  emit -> execute plans and restore prefixes
```

`Document` stores plans by node, preserving existing `EmitPlan` variants. Planning retains source spans, normalized pieces, token measurements, container boundaries, prefixes, and hard breaks. Finalization records line breaks, escapes, and child plans, then releases recognition drafts. Required decoded buffers stay with their child plans. Paragraphs, lists, definition lists, blockquotes, footnotes, rich/nested containers, and embedded Markdown consume these plans. Headings and tables retain normalized results from their existing algorithms.

Finalization propagates late file directives, front-matter options, and template delimiters before emission. Explicit targets still validate when encountered, preserving error/skip precedence while retaining successful support plans. Child skip flags, fragment defaults, external formatter execution, and existing line cleanup keep their semantics, including fragments' omission of top-level Markdown cleanup.

The Rust parse/finalize/emit interface transfers ownership: `ParsedDocument` exposes read-only inspection and nested skip; consuming finalization makes the source, tree, and policy private to `PreparedDocument`. Emission accepts no replacement source or policy. Eight temporary compiler checks confirm this boundary.

Validation compares this change with the recorded main baseline using Rust 1.98.1, identical release settings, and separate build directories. `scripts/check.sh` passed: formatting, Clippy, **608 Rust, 153 external, and 57 editor tests**. CI passed. Four test files mechanically adapt ownership calls; inputs, assertions, expected outputs, and allocation bounds are unchanged. Fixtures, snapshots, harnesses, inline tests, behavior documentation, CLI/configuration defaults, dependencies, toolchains, and CI are unchanged.

Temporary runners made **5,928 comparisons against main with zero mismatches** in stdout bytes, stderr, or exit status: 5,820 CLI first/second-pass comparisons and 108 parse/finalize/emit comparisons. Coverage includes fixtures, wrapping modes and canonicalization, nesting to depth 64, footnotes, code/math/links/attributes/HTML, existing templates/shortcodes, whitespace and hard breaks, LF/CRLF/CR, narrow widths, malformed inputs and fallbacks, late directives/custom delimiters/front matter, and Markdown in YAML/Python/R. Main's five known non-idempotent YAML inline cases remain unchanged; external formatters use controlled configurations.

Instrumentation covered **2,811 execution scopes across 2,910 CLI inputs**. Direct and indirect Markdown parser/scanner, fragment formatter, block-start recognizer, finalization, and prepared-tree construction counts were zero during emission. The 19 source-buffer constructions came from unchanged YAML indentation helpers. Instrumented outputs matched ordinary execution; verification parses remain outside these scopes.

Default-wrap measurements on an Apple M4 Max used 36 runtime samples each for main and this change, in alternating-order rounds. A separate allocator measured peak live heap above the pre-call level, not RSS; input/output digests matched and external formatters were disabled.

| Workload                   | Input bytes | Time, main → this change | Peak heap MB, main → this change | Allocations, main → this change |
| -------------------------- | ----------: | -----------------------: | -------------------------------: | ------------------------------: |
| Large paragraph            |   3,712,001 |       174.59 → 110.42 ms |                  52.115 → 26.825 |             2,583,271 → 157,178 |
| Rich nested containers     |     608,000 |         24.25 → 22.86 ms |                    2.618 → 9.676 |               444,847 → 403,269 |
| Explicit-target containers |     104,000 |           3.42 → 1.62 ms |                    0.586 → 1.507 |                 76,843 → 27,662 |
| Paragraphs with links      |     145,810 |           5.71 → 5.38 ms |                    0.576 → 1.228 |                 38,437 → 33,175 |

Allocations fell in all four workloads, but retained container/link plans increased peak memory over main. Some none/sentence/YAML elapsed-time measurements were 1–3% slower. Paragraph/container allocation and peak-heap growth remained approximately linear over 4× and 16× input sizes; these measurements do not establish zero CPU cost.

Planning still performs source-line indexing, recognition and normalization, template/raw-semantics checks, link splitting, and block-start scans. Changed planning policy can require reparsing retained child buffers because initial options affect target rejection and front-matter handling. Output verification retains its validation parse. This is not a literal two-walk implementation.

title: Preserve table alignment and make source widths configurable
description:
Add `table-widths=fit|preserve` so authors can choose whether Yamark computes Markdown table widths from their contents or retains the widths in the source. The setting applies to supported pipe, simple, grid, and multiline tables.

- `fit` remains the default. It intentionally prioritizes source readability by shrinking excessive widths and adding space to cramped columns. Fitting can change Pandoc's rendered table proportions and wrapping.
- `preserve` is opt-in. It retains source widths while still formatting cell contents. This can also retain excessive or cramped spacing. For pipe tables, it retains delimiter lengths and individual row widths, including rows whose borders were not aligned originally.

Source widths can reflect deliberate rendering choices or incidental spacing; Yamark cannot reliably infer which was intended. The option lets authors state that intent explicitly while retaining content-based sizing as the default.

The option controls widths. Column alignment is retained automatically in both modes, fixing cases where formatting lost the alignment encoded by the table syntax. Both modes also retain multiline cell breaks. Use the existing `fmt: skip` directive when the entire source layout must stay intact.

Authors can select the width policy at several scopes:

- One table: place `<!-- fmt: table-widths=preserve scope=next -->` immediately before it.
- A whole document: use `<!-- fmt: table-widths=preserve scope=file -->`.
- Subsequent tables: use `<!-- fmt: table-widths=preserve scope=from-here -->`; a later `<!-- fmt: table-widths=fit scope=from-here -->` resumes fitting.
- Front matter: set `table-widths: preserve` under `editor_options.markdown`.
- Repository configuration: set `table_widths = "preserve"` under `[format]` in `yamark.toml`.
- Command line: `yamark format --table-widths preserve report.qmd`.

For Markdown embedded in YAML, Python, or R, the setting can accompany the target marker: `# fmt: markdown table-widths=preserve`.

Scoped directives override document front matter; front matter overrides CLI flags; explicit CLI flags override `yamark.toml`; otherwise the default is `fit`.

All examples below show Markdown source. Each output was generated independently from the displayed input:

- **Before this PR:** Yamark built from the current base branch, `main` at `a6455ed`.
- **After this PR, default `fit`:** PR build `46b0e08`.
- **After this PR, `preserve`:** the same PR build with `--table-widths preserve`.

Both builds use `yamark format --wrap 72 --stdin-file-path example.qmd`. HTML width percentages below come from Quarto 1.10.18's bundled Pandoc, running `quarto pandoc --from markdown --to html --columns 72` on each input and output.

**Simple table alignment**

The input centers the second column. Before this PR, formatting loses that alignment. After this PR, both modes retain it automatically; `fit` also removes excess width.

**Input before formatting:**

```text
A           B
-----  ------------
x           y
```

**Output from main before this PR:**

```text
A    B
---  ---
x    y
```

**Output from this PR with default fit:**

```text
A     B
---  ---
x     y
```

**Output from this PR with --table-widths preserve:**

```text
A           B
-----  ------------
x           y
```

**Excessive grid width**

Before and after this PR, default formatting shrinks the source table and changes Pandoc's HTML table width from 19% to 11%. Selecting `preserve` keeps the source widths and the 19% HTML width.

**Input before formatting:**

```text
+------+------+
| A    | B    |
+======+======+
| x    | y    |
+------+------+
```

**Output from main, also the output from this PR with default fit:**

```text
+---+---+
| A | B |
+===+===+
| x | y |
+---+---+
```

**Output from this PR with --table-widths preserve:**

```text
+------+------+
| A    | B    |
+======+======+
| x    | y    |
+------+------+
```

**Cramped grid width**

Before and after this PR, default formatting adds space around the headers and changes Pandoc's HTML table width from 15% to 21%. Selecting `preserve` keeps the 15% width, including headers touching the borders.

**Input before formatting:**

```text
+----+-----+
|Name|Value|
+====+=====+
| x  | y   |
+----+-----+
```

**Output from main, also the output from this PR with default fit:**

```text
+------+-------+
| Name | Value |
+======+=======+
| x    | y     |
+------+-------+
```

**Output from this PR with --table-widths preserve:**

```text
+----+-----+
|Name|Value|
+====+=====+
| x  | y   |
+----+-----+
```

**Multiline table width**

Before and after this PR, default formatting reduces the source widths and changes Pandoc's HTML table width from 33% to 14%. Selecting `preserve` keeps the source widths and the 33% HTML width.

**Input before formatting:**

```text
Before.

----------  ----------
A           B
----------  ----------
x           y
----------  ----------
```

**Output from main, also the output from this PR with default fit:**

```text
Before.

---  ---
A    B
---  ---
x    y
---  ---
```

**Output from this PR with --table-widths preserve:**

```text
Before.

----------  ----------
A           B
----------  ----------
x           y
----------  ----------
```

The public Rust API adds `FormatOptions.markdown_table_widths` and `MarkdownTableWidths::{Fit, Preserve}`. CLI help, directive examples, configuration references, and release notes document the two modes and their precedence.

Internally, simple and multiline tables share column parsing and emission so alignment and widths are handled together. Grid alignment stays in border colons, avoiding indentation that Pandoc could interpret as code. Table parsing also handles headerless endings, tab stops, and Unicode column boundaries according to Pandoc's rules.

The shared check launcher now resolves current Ruff and py-yaml12 releases, the external runner declares Ruff, and Pages installs the latest Ruff.

title: Add read-only formatting and JSON-to-YAML previews
description:
## Summary

Yamark formatting is source-language-preserving and safe to apply back to a document. This change adds a separate, explicit projection path for inspecting or converting JSON-family data as YAML without making JSON files formatting targets. It also adds read-only editor previews for both that projection and the existing Format Document pipeline.

## User-facing changes

- Add `yamark to-yaml --stdin-file-path PATH` for JSON, JSONC, JSON5, JSONL, and NDJSON. It reads stdin, writes formatted YAML to stdout, and uses the original suffix only to select the input grammar.
- Add `Yamark: View JSON as YAML` and `Yamark: Preview Format Document` to the VS Code and Positron extension. Both use the current editor buffer and open a read-only virtual document without changing the source.
- Keep JSON-family files excluded from Format Document and format-on-save. The YAML projection does not run embedded formatters or the configured next formatter; the native preview uses the same formatting stages as Format Document.

## Internal changes

- Add dedicated JSON/JSONC and JSON5 adapters before Yamark's normal YAML layout pass. They preserve comments where supported, member order, duplicate keys, scalar meaning, and JSONL document boundaries while producing valid YAML.
- Share virtual-document cache and lifecycle plumbing between the two editor commands while retaining separate operation boundaries. Generation tracking prevents an older concurrent refresh from replacing newer preview content.
- Add dialect, diagnostic, allocation, pathological-input, extension-lifecycle, and documentation coverage, plus a provenance-preserving complete benchmark runner under `tools/bench`.

## Notes

Controlled same-host comparisons found no repeatable regression in the regular format path, with identical formatter output hashes. The release binary grows from 3,583,296 to 3,942,496 bytes, an increase of 359,200 bytes (10.0%).
